title: Computer components and what they do

spans.alt: Computer components and what they do
spans.caption: A diagram of the lesson’s key ideas
ASUS motherboard photo by Jacek Halicki (CC BY-SA 4.0)

spans.text: The motherboard connects the processor, memory, storage, and other parts. Data and power paths let them communicate. An incompatible component can prevent a computer from starting.

The central processing unit (CPU) carries out instructions and calculations. Random-access memory (RAM) temporarily holds data for programs in use. A full RAM can slow a computer down; RAM loses its contents when power is off.

A graphics processing unit (GPU) handles images and parallel calculations; some computers build it into the processor. Solid-state drives (SSD) and hard disk drives (HDD) keep files when power is off. SSDs are usually faster; HDDs use moving parts.

The power supply unit (PSU) converts electricity into forms the components can use. Fans and a heat sink carry heat away from the processor. Overheating can slow or shut down a computer. Turn it off and unplug it before opening a case or touching components.

BIOS/UEFI starts hardware during boot. A network adapter connects by cable or Wi-Fi. The screen, keyboard, mouse, and USB devices carry information between the user and computer. Each part has a different role, but the system works as a team.

If a computer will not start, check power and cables first; if it gets hot, make sure vents are clear. If the screen is blank, check the cable, display, and graphics device. Gather evidence and follow service instructions before replacing parts.
